Question: If Jenny from Forrest Gump had AIDS, why didn’t Forrest get it?
Answer: The theory that Jenny from Forrest Gump had AIDS has been a hot topic for years, and it’s pretty much accepted that her illness was likely related to HIV/AIDS, given the timeline and her lifestyle. But then, the big question—how the hell did Forrest not get it? The thing is, the movie never explicitly states what Jenny had, so we’re left to speculate. If she did have AIDS, there are a few possible explanations for why Forrest didn’t contract it. One possibility is that Forrest and Jenny might not have had s-e-x during the period when she was most infectious. HIV transmission isn’t guaranteed every time someone has unprotected s-e-x; it’s a risk, not a certainty. Also, depending on the timing of when Jenny contracted the virus, she might have already been in a stage where her viral load was lower when she and Forrest got together. Or, Forrest could’ve been just plain lucky. Sometimes people can be exposed and not contract the virus due to various factors, including genetic resistance, though that’s pretty rare. Ultimately, the movie is more of a romantic fantasy than a hard-hitting drama about disease. It’s about Forrest’s unwavering love and how he sees the world through a lens of pure, innocent devotion. So, the filmmakers probably didn’t want to dive into the nitty-gritty of HIV transmission—they were more focused on the emotional impact of Jenny’s death and the love she and Forrest shared. So, yeah, it’s a bit of movie magic, but that’s part of the charm, right? It’s one of those things you kind of have to roll with, even if it leaves you scratching your head.

Question: Did John Wayne dodge the Vietnam War like Clint Eastwood, or was he drafted and served as part of his duties like Lee Marvin?
Answer: John Wayne, the ultimate tough guy on screen, didn’t serve in Vietnam—or in any war, for that matter. But he wasn’t dodging anything. By the time Vietnam was in full swing, Wayne was already too old to be drafted. Born in 1907, he was pushing 60 when the Vietnam War was raging. And during World War II, he was in his mid-30s, which is kinda old by military standards for a new recruit. Now, some argue that he could’ve enlisted during WWII. At that time, he was making a name for himself in Hollywood, and while other stars like Jimmy Stewart and Lee Marvin went off to fight, Wayne stayed behind, cranking out patriotic movies that boosted morale. Some say he regretted not serving, and there’s even talk that he tried to enlist but was turned down due to his age and family responsibilities. Whether that’s true or just a way to soften the image is up for debate. Clint Eastwood, on the other hand, was drafted during the Korean War, but he never saw combat—he spent his service as a lifeguard at Fort Ord in California, which is a far cry from the front lines. And Lee Marvin? Yeah, he was the real deal. That guy was a Marine, fought in the Pacific during WWII, and got wounded in action. He was the kind of war hero Wayne often portrayed on screen. So, to wrap it up, John Wayne didn’t dodge the draft, but he also wasn’t in the heat of battle. He played the hero on screen, while guys like Lee Marvin were living it for real. It’s one of those cases where the lines between real life and Hollywood get a bit blurry...

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: Is Karen Gillan a "Karen" by nature?

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: Was Jim Parsons (Sheldon) selfish to leave The Big Bang Theory causing it to close down when it was still a hit show (one which left him five months of every year free to pursue other projects)?

Question: Are Anna Kendrick and Blake Lively feuding?

Question: What happened to Alicia Silverstone's career?

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: What actor and actress were a cinematic love affair for the ages?
Answer: When it comes to cinematic love affairs, one couple that still leaves everyone swooning is Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman in Casablanca. Name: Mr Shelby
Question: In Black Swan, what really happened in the last hospital scene with Nina and Beth?
Answer: That last hospital scene in Black Swan with Nina and Beth? It's one of those moments that makes you question everything—like, "Did I miss something, or did this just go full-on mind-bending?" So, Nina, our perfectly imperfect ballerina, visits Beth, who’s basically her idol turned cautionary tale. It’s like the movie is toying with your mind just as much as Nina’s mind is toying with her. Beth represents Nina’s worst fears—becoming obsolete, forgotten, or worse, a cautionary tale like Beth. The hospital scene blurs the line between reality and hallucination, leaving you wondering what’s real and what’s not. In short... Nina’s sanity is crumbling faster than a stale cookie, and this scene is just another nail in her mental coffin. Did she actually stab Beth? Probably not. But in her twisted mind, anything’s possible.

Question: What are some interesting stories about the actress Brie Larson?

First of all, did you know she started as a teen pop star? Yep, in the early 2000s, she released a pop album called Finally Out of P.E.—a title that’s both cringe and totally relatable. Another fun tidbit: when she was cast as Captain Marvel, the internet trolls went nuts. They criticized everything from her acting to her facial expressions (because, you know, people have so much time to nitpick). But Larson didn’t back down—she’s been super vocal about gender equality and representation in Hollywood, which has earned her both hardcore fans and a fair share of haters. She even did some of her own stunts in Captain Marvel to shut down critics who doubted her action-hero skills. So, yeah... Brie Larson’s story isn’t just about winning awards and looking good on red carpets. She’s faced the grind, almost quit, and still came out swinging. Total badass, if you ask me...

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: Did Tom Hanks or Denzel Washington have any professional backlash for doing the movie "Philadelphia"?

Sure, there were probably a few people who weren’t thrilled about it, but that didn’t stop these two legends from getting even bigger and better roles afterward. So, not only did they not face backlash, but they also got a ton of respect and recognition for having the guts to take on such an important and timely project.

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: Did Anne Hathaway ruin her career?

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: *spoilers! * Why did certain group of people make son of Satan (Devil) enter into human world, in Rosemary's Baby?

So, why did this twisted group of people, aka the cult, decide it was a good idea to bring the son of Satan into the world? Well, the short answer is: they’re batshit crazy, and they believe they’re doing something grand... like ushering in a new age of evil. Name: Mr Shelby
Question: When and how did Voldemort get Nagini?

In this form, she ends up on Voldemort’s radar, and let’s just say he’s not the type to miss out on such a powerful, magical creature. Nagini becomes his trusted ally, used for everything from assassinations to carrying a piece of his soul like the twisted version of a Horcrux necklace. It’s a disturbing relationship, to say the least. Voldemort doesn’t have friends, but if he did, Nagini would be the closest thing—albeit in a really sick and twisted way.

Name: Mr Shelby
Question: How did Kate Winslet feel about Titanic?

There are stories of him kicking a guy so hard that he flew back several feet. That’s not just movie magic; that’s raw, undeniable power. He was a philosopher of martial arts, constantly evolving and adapting his techniques. This dedication made him not just a master of physical combat but also a thinker who could out-strategize his opponents. And let’s not forget his impact on popular culture. Bruce Lee brought martial arts to the mainstream, inspiring countless people to take up the discipline. He broke down racial barriers in Hollywood, proving that an Asian actor could be a leading man and an international superstar. So, was Bruce Lee as good as he claimed to be? Hell yeah, he was. He didn’t just live up to the hype; he defined it. His legacy as a martial artist, actor, and cultural icon continues to inspire and influence people around the world.
